related_questions.question: What is the new travel requirement for the UK?

text_blocks.snippet: Starting January 8, 2025, the UK requires an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) for travelers from visa-exempt countries, including the U.S., for most visits up to six months, including those transiting through the UK. This authorization is linked to the traveler's passport and is valid for two years.
snippet_highlighted_words: an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) for travelers from visa-exempt countries, including the U.S., for most visits up to six months, including those transiting through the UK

list.title: What is it?
list.snippet: The ETA is a digital authorization that allows eligible travelers to enter the UK for tourism, short-term business, family visits, or transit purposes.

list.title: Who needs it?
list.snippet: U.S. citizens, as well as citizens of other visa-exempt countries, who do not have a UK visa or UK residency will need an ETA.

list.title: Why is it needed?
list.snippet: The ETA is part of the UK's efforts to enhance border security and streamline the entry process for visitors.

list.title: How to apply:
list.snippet: Travelers can apply for the ETA online through the UK government website or the UK ETA mobile app.

list.title: Cost and validity:
list.snippet: The ETA costs £10 and is valid for two years or until the passport expires, whichever comes first.

list.title: Important note:
list.snippet: Travelers must secure the ETA before they travel, as it is needed to board their flight.
